(i) a Schmidt decomposition can be experimentally established with only local measurements and filtering, and (ii) the same method can be used to detect entanglement.

we have experimentally demonstrated a Schmidt decomposition of an unknown state and a state-independent entanglemnt witness.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entanglement of a given unknown state is revealed by the Schmidt decomposition, which in the case of pure states can be established by local filtering of the measurement outcomes.
we have developed an experimental method for Schmidt decomposition and entanglement detection that does not rely on any prior knowledge of the state and is therefore state independent.
we have developed a new approach to detect entanglement in a state-independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Schmidt decomposition is not only a theoretical concept, but can also be established experimentally, even for mixed states, which is a crucial ingredient for the detection of entanglement.
the Schmidt decomposition can be experimentally obtained from a small number of projective measurements.
